text:
Droit de la famille — 22578

2022 QCCS 1415

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTREAL

No.:

500-12-333329-161

DATE:

April 13, 2022

_____________________________________________________________________

BY

THE HONOURABLE

KAREN KEAR-JODOIN, J.S.C.

_____________________________________________________________________

A. W.

Father

v.

D. WO.

Mother

_____________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT on modification of
parental time and child support

_____________________________________________________________________

1.

Introduction

[
1
]

The parties are the parents of X 9 years of age
and Y presently 7 years of age. A judgment of divorce (“
Divorce Judgment
”)
was rendered on June 26, 2018. The Court ratified a Consent on Accessory
Measures dated January 9, 2018 which provided, among others, that the parties
share custody of the minor children on an alternating week to week basis.

[
2
]

The Divorce Judgment also ratified a second
agreement namely Final Consent Agreement signed by the parties on June 26, 2018
which addressed issues such as the children’s choice of school, activities,
special expenses and the adjustment of child support.

[
3
]

On March 31, 2021, Mother instituted an Application
to seek the adjustment of child support retroactive to January 2019. She
requested that, in the event of Father’s failure to file a child support
determination form, the Court impute an income to him. Mother further requested
that Father transmit to her his income tax returns each year and to advise of
any change in his financial situation within 30 days of any such change.

[
4
]

On June 7, 2021, Father instituted a Demand to
modify custody and child support. To this end, he requested the determination
of child support and that an income be imputed to Mother. He requested that she
assume 100% of the cost of daycare and other expenses relating to the
children’s attendance at Elementary School A while the children are in her
care. He further requested an order to authorize both parties to attend the
children’s medical appointments. Last but not least, he contests Mother’s Application
for retroactive adjustment of child support to January 2019.

2.

What must the court decide?

[
5
]

The issues that the Court must determine are as
follows:

5.1.

Has there been a material change of
circumstances to warrant the modification of parental time as set out in the
Divorce Judgment rendered on June 26, 2018? If so, what modality of parental
time is in the best interest of X and Y?

5.2.

Should the Court set out modalities with respect
to the children’s medical appointments?

5.3.

Should child support be adjusted retroactive to
January 2019?

5.4.

What is Mother’s income? What is Father’s
income? Should the Court impute income to either parent?

5.5.

Should there be any modification as to the parties’
respective obligation towards the payment of special expenses for the minor
children?

3.

Background

[
6
]

The parties were married on May 10, 2014 and
separated on September 26, 2016. Following the separation, the parties shared
custody of the children. Father allegedly instituted divorce proceedings on
December 13, 2016 following Mother’s unwillingness to return the children to Father
after her parental time with them.

[
7
]

Mother raised serious allegations against Father
stating that he was physically abusive to her. She asserted that she was a
victim of domestic violence. Two criminal accusations were laid against Father,
the first one in 2015 and another in 2017. Father was acquitted of the first
charge and the second charge was ultimately withdrawn.

[
8
]

On January 9, 2018, the parties reached a
Consent on Accessory Measures. The provisions relating to custody relevant to this
dispute are as follows:

11.       The Parties shall continue to have shared custody of their
children, X and Y, as agreed in the Interim Judgment signed on February 9
th
,
2017, until July 6
th
, 2018;

12.       The parties agree and undertake that starting July 6
th
,
2018, they shall continue to have shared custody of their children, X and Y, on
a weeklv alternating basis, exchanging the children every Friday in the
morning, at the Daycare Center, at the latest by 11:00 a.m.;

13.       In the event of a holiday or pedagogical day, the Parties
agree to exchange the children the day before or the day after so as to extend
the weekend, accordingly;

14.       The Parties agree that any additional time of custody with
one parent shall be adjusted in favour of the other parent in a collaborative
manner between the Parties;

15.       The Parties agree that the principle means of
communication between the Parties shall be via email, unless it is a case of
emergency involving the children, being understood that the communication is
only about the children;

[
9
]

The Consent on Accessory Measures provided that
Father pay child support of $180 per month as well as all day care expenses for
both children. Child support was to be subsequently revisited as of July 1,
2018.

[
10
]

On June 26, 2018, the parties signed a second
agreement, the Final Consent, whereby the parties agreed that X and eventually Y
shall attend School A in Town A. Child support was increased to $350 per month
andFather would assume all costs relating to same including daycare, school
supplies, hot lunches, school uniforms, field trips and other school
activities. The parties further agreed that the children shall attend School B.

[
11
]

The relevant provisions of the final consent
agreement relating to the adjustment of child support are as follows:

8.         The Father shall pay the Mother a child support payment
in the amount of $350 per month, beginning July 1
st
, 2018, as well
as the daycare expenses of Y which shall continue to be exclusively assumed by
the Father.

9.         The Parties agree to participate on an equal (50/50) basis
as concerns the following special expenses:

a)

Dental;

b)

Medical;

c)

Seasonal clothing.

10.       All other special expenses shall be assumed by the parent
who has contracted it without the consent of the other parent;

10a)     The Mother shall have the custody of the children for the
week-end of June 29, 2018 until July 4
th
, 2018.

[
12
]

Despite an acrimonious start to their
litigation, once the Divorce Judgment was rendered, the parties appear to have
been able to put aside their own interests and to collaborate, all in the best
interest of X and Y. However, in April 2020, the situation rapidly deteriorated.
The conflict intensified.

[
13
]

Father started to seriously question Mother’s
mental stability and her ability to provide a safe and secure environment for
the children.

[
14
]

Mother, on the other hand, sees no problem. She
is a good mother, and the boys love her. She portrays herself as a victim of
domestic violence and psychological abuse having been harassed and stalked
relentlessly not only by Father, her family and by “
men with lots of money
who do bad things
”.

[
15
]

At trial, both parties were self-represented.
Father called as his witness Mother’s former boyfriend with whom she resided in
2020.

4.

Has there been a material change of
circumstances to warrant the modification of parental time as set out in the
divorce judgment rendered on June 26, 2018.If so, What modality of parental
time is in the best interest of X and Y?

4.1

The law

[
16
]

The
Divorce Act
sets out the Court’s
authority to change a parenting order:
[1]

17

(1)
A court of competent jurisdiction may make an order varying,
rescinding or suspending, retroactively or prospectively, […]

(b)
a parenting order or any provision of one, on application by

(i)
either or both
former spouses, or

(ii)
a person, other
than a former spouse, who is a parent of the child, stands in the place of a
parent or intends to stand in the place of a parent;

[…]

(5)
Before the court makes a variation
order in respect of a parenting order or contact order, the court shall satisfy
itself that there has been a change in the circumstances of the child since the
making of the order or the last variation order made in respect of the order,
or of an order made under subsection 16.5(9).

[
17
]

To determine an Application to modify a parental
time order, the Court must rely on the principles and process as set out in
Gordon

v.
Goertz
.
[2]

[
18
]

The onus is on the parent seeking to modify the
existing order to establish that, on the balance of probabilities, there is a
material change that affects or is likely to affect the best interest of the
child namely in the condition, means, needs or circumstances of the child and/or
the ability of the parents to meet those needs.

[
19
]

The change must have occurred since the making
of the order. Such change must materially affect the child, the parents or
both. It is only once a parent has established a material change of
circumstances that the parties then share the burden to demonstrate where the best
interest of the child lie.

[
20
]

Thereafter, the Court is guided by one pivotal
consideration namely the best interest of the child. The notion of best
interest must be assessed from the perspective of the child rather than that of
the parents. The Court must take into all relevant circumstances pertaining to
the child’s needs and the ability of each parent to meet those needs.
[3]

[
21
]

In this matter, a review of the modalities of
parental time is warranted for the following reasons.

[
22
]

Father submits that Mother’s mental health has
deteriorated to the extent that she is no longer capable to provide a stable
and secure environment for the children. He raises numerous concerns which
include that:

22.1.

Mother has changed residences no less than seven
times since 2017 and that she continues to refuse to disclose to Father the
residence of the children.

22.2.

Mother has no insight as to the needs of the
children and has placed her needs before theirs.

22.3.

Mother has exposed the children to unhealthy
relationships and unsuitable environments.

22.4.

Mother has isolated herself and the children
from friends and family.

[
23
]

Father further asserts that Mother made repeated
complaints to the police and to the Director of Youth Protection, none of which
have been retained. He believes that Mother suffers from some form of mental
illness.

[
24
]

Father’s concerns are shared by the maternal
grandmother and the Mother’s sister. Both support Father’s request for
exclusive parenting time.

[
25
]

The maternal grandmother states in her solemn
declaration dated June 7, 2021:
[4]

4.         She contacted me by email to let me know that I will
never see her or my grandchildren X & Y ever again.

5.         She threatened that if I tried to contact her or my
grandchildren, she would call the police.

6.         I do not understand what happened to my daughter, but I
am very worried for her and my grandchildren.

7.         I do believe my daughter needs help somehow.

[
26
]

Mother’s sister states in her solemn declaration
dated June 3, 2021 the following:
[5]

4.         I am extremely concern (sic) for my nephews’ well-being
when they are with their mother.

10.       I believe my sister is not currently fit to take care of
her children. She has cut everyone out of her life who tried to help her,
leaving the kids exposed to her alone, with no other adult to turn too (sic) in
case of need;

12.        D… has had and (sic) extreme
shift in attitude in the past couple of years and she pushed everyone out when
they tried to help her;

15.       D… was a wonderful mother, but these past years has shown
a huge irresponsibility to her children. I know my sister inside out, and I
know without a doubt that she is going through a psychosis episode that started
about 4 years ago, it is getting worse not better. We love D… very much and
want to help her as she is completely unreasonable. This is why I fear for the kids.
She calls the police, social services and reports on everyone that she thinks
is there to hurt her or kidnap the kids. D… may seem as a lair (sic), but
actually needs immediate help/hospitalizafion for her sake and the safety of
kids.

19.       X and Y frequently ask me things that are troubling’ “Why
are you all trying to hurt mom? Is dad bad? Etc. These are just small talk
information that these young children speak to me about, and when I ask why
they are asking this the response is mostly “I don’t know” and even if I try to
let them know how much we love them, and that nobody here is trying to hurt
anyone, and that everyone in the family is nice, the conversation seems to end
there.

[
27
]

In view of the foregoing, the Court finds that
there has been a material change of circumstances to warrant a review of the
provisions relating to the parental time of the children.

4.2

What modality of parental time is in the best interest of X and Y?

[
28
]

The Court is guided by the factors set out at

article 33
of the
Civil Code of Québec
which reads as follows:
[6]

33.
Every
decision concerning a child shall be taken in light of the child’s interests
and the respect of his rights.

Consideration is given, in addition
to the moral, intellectual, emotional and physical needs of the child, to the
child’s age, health, personality and family environment, and to the other
aspects of his situation.

[
29
]

The Court of appeal has set out other factors
[7]

which may come into consideration when determining parental time, such as:

•

The parental capacity of each parent;

•

The relationship between the child and each parent;

•

The need for a stable environment;

•

The existing custody and access arrangements;

•

The environment suggested by the parents;

•

The wish to avoid separating siblings;

•

The physical and mental health of the children as well as the
parents’;

•

The parents’ life habits, if they have a direct impact on the
children;

•

The availability of each parent;

•

The desirability to ensure as much contact with each parent as is
consistent with the best interests of the child;

•

The expressed wish of the child, depending on his or her age.

[
30
]

No factor is determinant. All factors must be
considered globally and are specific to each case.

[
31
]

When addressing the viability of shared parental
time certain factors must be considered more particularly, including those
already mentioned:
[8]

➢

the interest and stability of the child;

➢

the parental capacity of the parents;

➢

the absence of conflicts between the parents and
their capacity to communicate in a functional manner;

➢

the proximity or remoteness of the parents’
domiciles.

[
32
]

The Court concludes that shared parental time is
no longer viable. The Court has particular concerns with respect to Mother’s
parental capacity and the stability of the children. The best interests of the
children dictate that Father have the majority of parental time for the
following reasons.

[
33
]

Mother describes Father as a chronic verbal and
psychological abuser. She “
ran
” from the marriage in 2017 and, since the
separation, he has incessantly stalked and harassed her. She further alleges
that he is a manipulator who has turned her family against her. According to
Mother, Father has sabotaged all off her efforts to secure employment and to
launch her business.

[
34
]

Mother is allegedly so fearful of Father that she
refuses to disclose her address. She asserts that, as a result of his abuse and
the toxic relationship Mother has with her family and Father, she must remain
isolated to remain “
safe
” and “
sane
”. However, the difficulty
with Mother’s narrative as to the abuse she has suffered at the hands of Father
and the maternal family, is that she was unable to offer a scintilla of
evidence to support any of her assertions of victimhood.

[
35
]

Allegations of domestic violence must always be
taken seriously. However, Mother was unable to provide details when asked by
the Court. Mother spoke in generalities and offered no cogent examples of
incidence of physical or psychological abuse by Father or by her family.

[
36
]

Mother alleged that Father stalked her in order
to find her location at a Women’s Shelter. This was untrue. Mother
inadvertently revealed the address of the shelter on one of her many social
media posts.
[9]

Her perception of Father as dangerous and abusive permeates throughout her
social media posting. She posts libelous statements such as Father threatening
to kill her
[10]

or that he had alleged that she had sex with the children, in an effort to
obtain their custody.

[
37
]

There is no evidence to support these
assertions. Father is at a loss to understand Mother’s conduct. He queries if she
actually believes her allegations or if she is simply attempting to hurt him.
If she believes such accusations, Mother has serious psychological difficulties.
In either case, the long-term consequences of such an inaccurate, albeit delusional
perception of Father shall clearly adversely affect his relationship with the
children.

[
38
]

Mother’s confused perception of Father is
contrary to the best interests of the children. It is difficult to believe that
Mother’s incessant narrative is not transmitted consciously or unconsciously to
the children. The Court underscores one example of a Facebook post dated
November 12, 2021 where Mother states as follows:

Today my son said he is scared of
his father this is the millionth time I called child protection services we’ve
been at this for over five years with this. The system needs to change not the
climate […] psychological abuse is worse than physical abuse it is not
understood or educated enough in our schools or society.

[
39
]

The Court doubts Mother’s assertion that she
does not share with the children the perceived abuse that she suffered by
Father or her family. She, however, affirms that the children are smart and
know what they see. Mother adds that they have allegedly been exposed to
physical violence.

[
40
]

Father is concerned by Mother’s activity on
social media which posts are available to the public.
[11]
Understandably, this has
caused Father’s embarrassment. The unsubstantiated allegations posts can be
seen by parents of children who attend the same school as X and Y.

[
41
]

More importantly, Father worries as to how the social
media posts may have affected the children. The Court can’t help but wonder if
the parents who view these posts are reluctant to have their children play with
X and Y.

[
42
]

Mother places her need in priority to the
children needs. Mother perceives herself as a perpetual victim. Rather than
securing appropriate accommodations for the children, she chose to remain at a
Women’s Shelter from October 2020 to September 2021. What is of concern to the Court
is Mother’s description that “
Women’s Shelters are a wonderful place for
children […] like a castle
”.

[
43
]

Mother explains that the Shelter carries on
workshops with the children. The session consists of posters on the wall to
educate the women and the children in order that they understand the subtleties
of psychological abuse. She informed the Court that she wants the children to
be aware of the covert ways of psychological abuse. She fears that they will be
kidnapped. Mother states:

In 2020 the harassment by email and
by phone calls continued. I did not feel safe living alone with two small
children and an entire ex-family who is trying to find ways to hurt me
emotionally with my children, socially with my network, and mentally with forms
of psychological abuse. My location services are turned off. The children are
no longer allowed to wear GPS tracking devices to my home. I changed my cell
phone number and my email addresses several times. I blocked everyone on social
media that was related to both of my ex-families. Sometimes I see them pop up
with a new name to check up on me. My email and other online accounts were
hacked and manipulated.

[
44
]

Mother emphasizes that she is exhausted trying
to keep a safe environment for her children. She is simply trying to break the
cycle of violence and she wants to show her children that there is another way.

[
45
]

Mother has absolutely no insight that the
message she transmits to the children, not only concerning Father, but that the
world at large is not a safe place. This is a very heavy burden for young
children as was revealed by X. The child recently confided in Father: ”
Daddy
I have a hard life
” and asked if he could stay with him.

[
46
]

There is no doubt that the children’ lives have
been difficult in recent years. They have had no stability while in Mother’s
care. They relocated on seven occasions living approximately one year at a Woman
Shelter.

[
47
]

In 2020, the children resided with Mother’s new
business partner and boyfriend. It was a very unhealthy relationship. At trial,
Mother described her boyfriend as her “
protector
”, allegedly from
Father. The boyfriend assumed the responsibility of all communications between Mother
and Father. He interfered in decisions relating to the children including those
concerning their medical care. He threatened and harassed Father and members of
his family indicating that his family and entourage were associated with the
criminal underworld.

[
48
]

He stated in his email to Father dated April 10,
2020:
[12]

D… is now a member of my family the
house of X and she is protected. Who do you want to contact in my family? I
will give you their numbers if you wish, let’s start with my brothers and
cousins.

[
49
]

He then attached thereto a link to various press
releases relating to his family’s alleged criminal activity. Father would have
been well justified to file a criminal complaint against him.

[
50
]

Mother’s relationship with her boyfriend ended
in October 2020 following an incident of alleged domestic violence. Father was only
advised of the incident by the Director of Youth Protection because the
children had been instructed to keep the incident a secret.
[13]

[
51
]

The events raise red flags concerning Mother’s
parental judgment.

[
52
]

First, why would Mother subjects the children to
cohabit with an individual with apparent ties to persons involved in criminal
activity?

[
53
]

Second, and more importantly, Mother’s effort to
conceal the incident from Father and to tell the children to keep a secret from
him demonstrates, to say the least, poor parental judgment.

[
54
]

Mother has failed to give priority to the
children’s education. Although Father notes an improvement since he instituted
his demand, the children often arrive late to school or not at all. By letter
dated February 10, 2020 the school expressed concern.
[14]
During a 5-month period, namely
September to February, X had arrived late to school on 35 occasions and was
absent 7 days without justification.

[
55
]

Mother attempted, without success, to justify
her failure to bring the children to school on time or at all stating that she
suffers from migraine headaches.

[
56
]

There are other irritants.

[
57
]

The parties do not share the same view with
regards to medical care for the children. Mother believes that Father does not
provide appropriate medication for X. Father replies that he follows the
instructions of the child’s pediatrician and is concerned that Mother may
overmedicate the child. X reports to Father “
Mommy tells me I am very sick
”.

[
58
]

Mother’s boyfriend intervened and forwarded the
following email to Father:
[15]

Hello A…,

Make the Dr. Appointments yourself
and then follow that. If X gets sick because you cannot follow instructions, he
will not be coming here. We handed the boys over in good health and happy. The
lawyers will deal with that when the time comes … please use one and let me
know which one.

Go get the meds.

[
59
]

Mother complains that Father does not provide
appropriate hygiene. Father denies same and expresses concerns that Mother
continue to shower with the children.

[
60
]

Mother also complains that Father does not pay
certain special expenses of the children. Father complains that Mother
overcharges him for special expenses by failing to advise him of any government
benefits.
[16]

[
61
]

Last but not least, Mother fails to accept any
responsibility for her current financial situation. She is unemployed. She
presently receives welfare assistance. She states: “
my present financial
situation is due to the Applicant’s constant harassment and me having to gain
some peace
”. Mother resorted to a Facebook call for donations for clothing
and food for the children including such items as toothpaste, juice boxes and
snacks for school.
[17]

[
62
]

At trial, Mother did not appear to appreciate
the gravity of Father’s concerns nor of his request for the majority of parental
time of the children. Rather than focus on the on the children and their needs,
Mother’s testimony centered on her alleged victimhood of perceived abuse at the
hands of her family and the patriarchal society’s lack of understanding of
abuse. Mother perceives herself as a crusader for all women who are victims of
domestic abuse. Her first priority should be her children.

[
63
]

When the Court asked about her future plans, Mother
stated that after 39 years of abuse she considers herself an expert on domestic
abuse. She wants to teach women how to get out of this situation, to keep
saving women and to create beautiful and safe places for them.

[
64
]

Mother perceives herself as a good mother. She
sees no reason why shared parenting time should be modified. She asserts that
she has done nothing wrong. She is the victim. The children love her and they
know that she is always there for them.

[
65
]

The Court finds that Father is not motivated in
bad faith. He has a sincere and legitimate concern for the well-being of his
children. Father did not demonstrate anger at trial. Father’s testimony was
calm and reflective. He described the children in glowing terms. Despite the
difficulties they have experienced during recent years, they have done very well
at school. X and Y are very bright. They are hard workers and are at the top of
their class. He described the interests of the children and how he encourages the
values of independence and education. He stimulates the children to pursue
their interests such as snowboarding, piano and jiu-jitsu.

[
66
]

Father has suitable accommodations for the
children in close proximity to their school and he works from home. He ensures
that the children have frequent contact with the maternal family with whom they
are very much attached.

[
67
]

It is clear to the Court that Father’s decision
to seek exclusive parenting time was a last resort. Father offered mediation on
no less than 5 occasions in 2020 and in 2021 all of which were refused or
remained unanswered.
[18]

At trial, Father stated he remained hopeful that shared custody could resume if
Mother receives the psychological care she requires. Father acknowledged that X
and Y love their Mother and was sensitive to the children’s reaction in the
event that he is granted the majority of parental time. He stated that he shall
provide them with the emotional support and, if necessary, obtain the necessary
therapeutic support for the children. He does not want to exclude Mother from
the lives of the children, he simply wishes that she obtain the help she needs.

[
68
]

All of the foregoing considerations favour Father
having the majority of parenting time of X and Y which shall commence on April
14, 2022. It is important that the children continue to have contact with
Mother as long as she refrains from any negative commentary concerning Father
and Mother’s family. If Mother continues to speak of Father in derogatory terms,
either in the presence of the children or in any manner which could ultimately
come to their knowledge of the children, Mother shall risk losing her parental
time.

[
69
]

The children shall be with Mother every
alternate weekend from Thursday after school until Monday morning at school and
on the following week from Thursday after school until Friday morning at
school. In addition to the foregoing, Mother shall have additional parenting
time as set out in the conclusions of this judgment.

[
70
]

Prior to the commencement of Mother’s parental
time with the children, she shall provide Father with written notice as to her
current address and telephone number. Moreover, Mother shall advise Father
immediately of any change of address prior to Mother’s relocation.

4.3

Should the Court set out modalities with respect to the children’s
medical appointments?

[
71
]

Notwithstanding that Father has the majority of
parental time, both parents continue to share parental authority and
decision-making responsibility for X and Y. Father shall provide Mother with
1-week written notice of any and all scheduled medical and or dental
appointments for the minor children.

[
72
]

Mother shall be free to attend said medical
and/or dental appointments. Should mother decline to attend said appointments,
Father shall provide to Mother a text message providing a brief resume of the
outcome of the appointment.

4.4

Should child support be adjusted retroactive to January 2019? What
is Mother’s income? What is Father’s income? Should the Court impute income to
either parent? Should there be any modification as to the parties’ respective
obligation towards the payment of special expenses for the minor children?

[
73
]

Article 17 (4)
of the
Divorce Act

provides that prior to the Court making a variation with respect to a child
support order, the Court must be satisfied that a change of circumstances as
provided for in the applicable guidelines has occurred since the making of the
child support order. Clearly, where there is a significant change with respect
to the modalities of parental time a review of child support is warranted.

[
74
]

Moreover, article 595 C.C.Q. authorizes the Court
to modify retroactively for 3 years preceding the institution of the Application
to modify which provides as follows:
[19]

595.
Child
support may be claimed for needs that existed before the application; however,
child support cannot be claimed for needs that existed more than three years
before the application, unless the debtor parent behaved in a reprehensible
manner towards the other parent or the child.

If the support is not claimed for a
child, it may nevertheless be claimed for needs that existed before the
application, but not for needs that existed more than one year before the
application; in such a case, the creditor must prove that it was in fact
impossible to act sooner, unless he put the debtor in default within one year
before the application, in which case support is awarded from the date of
default.

[
75
]

Article 446 C.P.C. also confers discretion upon
the court to impute income as follows:
[20]

446.
If the particulars in a prescribed
document are incomplete or contested, or in any circumstances it considers it
necessary, the court may supplement the information. The court may determine a
parent’s income by considering, among other things, the value of the parent’s
assets and the income they generate or could generate, as it considers
appropriate.

[
76
]

In 2017, when the divorce judgment was rendered
Father agreed to pay monthly child support of $350 per month based upon
Mother’s then admitted income of $25,766.53 and Father’s then admitted income
of $25,016.43.

[
77
]

When Mother filed her application to vary
accessory measures and child support on March 31, 2021 seeking the retroactive
adjustment of child support she alleged that she was without income. Mother
failed to file in the court record the relevant documentation such as her
income tax declarations and notice of assessment.

[
78
]

Mother has the burden of proof to establish a
change of income to justify the adjustment of child support. However, she
offered no evidence to establish her income for the taxation years 2019 to
2021. She has filed no income tax declarations nor provided the relevant
financial disclosure. Mother has not satisfied her burden to demonstrate that
there has been any significant change of her income nor any significant change
in Father’s income since the divorce judgment that was rendered in 2021.

[
79
]

Mother states that she is presently receiving
welfare benefits. However, there is evidence suggesting that Mother continues
to operate her business which shall be further addressed below. In the absence
of such evidence, the Court shall not retroactively adjust child support to
2019 as per Mother’s request.

[
80
]

Moving forward, what is the appropriate quantum
of child support?

[
81
]

The quantum of child support is determined in
consideration of the parties’ respective incomes, the number of children and
the modalities of parental time. In the present matter child support shall be
based upon Father having the majority of parental time with X and Y.

[
82
]

What is Father’s income? Father is a graphic
designer and is the sole shareholder of [Company A]. Mother did not contest
Father’s income for the years 2019 to 2021.

[
83
]

The Court finds that Father’s income for 2021
and anticipated income for 2022 remains approximately $25,000
per annum
.
The Court has reviewed the financial statements for [Company A] for the year
ending December 31, 2020. The Court notes that a portion of certain expenses of
the company may, to some degree, be incurred for Father’s personal benefit such
as meals, entertainment, travel, automotive, and office expenses which would
result in an increase in Father’s income. However, there is insufficient
evidence to enable the Court to quantify the portion of such expenses which may
be for Father’s benefit. The Court concludes that Father’s income for the
purposes of determining child support is $25,000
per annum
which is
consistent with his average income since 2018.

[
84
]

Father asks the Court to impute to Mother an annual
income of between $40,000 and $50,000. Father bases his estimate of Mother’s
proposed income on Mother’s sales in 2017. The court is unable to ascertain
from the information provided to the court Mother’s net income after payment of
expenses.

[
85
]

Mother is a professional interior designer. She
was served with a subpoena to bring her curriculum vitae. She did not bring
same. When asked why she did not bring the document to Court she simply states:
“
I am my C.V.
” Mother is very accomplished. She has two university
degrees. She is able to speak eight languages. She is called upon by Cegep A to
act as a judge for the interior design competitions. She considers herself as
an expert on domestic violence and is called upon to speak at international
conferences. It is difficult to reconcile Mother’s stellar qualifications and
her lack of employment. She blames Father for her inability to secure
employment. “
I have to stay isolated … it is safer for me”.

[
86
]

When asked about her future plans she said she
planned to continue saving women and creating safe spaces for them. She also
spoke of the thesis “written on my brain” and research on feminicide. She did
not appear to have any future plans to secure gainful employment. She does not
address how she may contribute to the payment of the financial needs of the
children.

[
87
]

Mother may, presently, to carry on business
under the name of [Company B]. She is listed on HOUZZ. Her hourly rate of four
virtual consultations is $288 per hour on site, consultations are at a cost of
$388 per hour. Her hourly rate after consultation is indicated to be $85 per
hour.

[
88
]

Father submitted as exhibit P-36 a series of
invoices totaling $9,532.98 during the period from February 3, 2020 to
September 1, 2020. Although the Court accepts the testimony of Mother’s
boyfriend with extreme caution, he confirmed that, during their cohabitation, Mother
had had six or seven projects including one in Town B.

[
89
]

Father also files exhibit P-19 a copy of an
image from Mother’s website stating “Scheduling Interior Design projects for
fall 2022. Waitlist now opened”. This may be no more than a marketing ploy but
leads the Court to suspect that Mother may be doing more than her blog “[Blog
A]”.

[
90
]

Child support is of public order. Parents have a
joint ongoing obligation to support their children. In order to meet their
obligations, each parent has a duty to earn what he or she is capable of
earning. A parent cannot avoid a child support obligation by either
unemployment or a self-induced reduction of income. It is time that Mother
accepts her responsibility to financially contribute to the children.

[
91
]

The Court shall impute to Mother an annual
income of $25,000 which the Court believes to be a conservative estimate as of her
capacity to earn. In order to give Mother sufficient time to secure employment,
child support shall only commence as of June 1, 2022.

[
92
]

There is in sufficient evidence to enable the Court
to adjudicate upon the payment of the special expenses of the children. No
evidence was presented with respect to the cost of their extracurricular
activities. The Court shall order the parties to share equally the cost of all
expenses including afterschool daycare, if necessary, medical and dental care
as well as prescription glasses for the children. The parties shall also share
the cost of all extracurricular activities of the children provided that the
expense has been preapproved by both parties, failing which the party who
incurs the cost for the extracurricular activity shall be solely responsible
for same.
